screenSummary.playArea: A burette of titrant hangs over a flask of analyte with an indicator. A pH meter can be dipped in the flask, and a chart plots the pH against the volume added.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose the sample, its concentration and volume, the titrant concentration and the indicator. Open the stopcock or add single drops, record burette readings in the notebook, and for the unknown acid enter and check its concentration.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Open the stopcock to start, then close it and add single drops as the colour starts to change.

controls.answer: Your concentration for the unknown acid

responses.flashPattern: A flash of {{color}} where the drop landed, fading as it mixes.
responses.newFlask: New flask of analyte, no titrant added.

screenSummary.playArea: The calculated titration curve, pH against volume of titrant, with markers at the half-equivalence and equivalence points, and below it the fraction of each acid–base species. A cursor marks one volume.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose the analyte, a second curve to compare, the concentrations, and what the charts show. Move the cursor or jump between key points; the readout gives the pH, region, concentrations and amounts there.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Jump between key points to see where pH equals pKa and where the equivalence points fall.

controls.cursor: Volume of titrant at the cursor

screenSummary.playArea: A row of tubes shows every indicator at the chosen pH, with a chart of their colour-change ranges. A breakdown shows the forms of the selected indicator. A titration curve shows where each indicator would change colour.
screenSummary.controlArea: Set the pH, pick an indicator to break down, and pick a titration to compare the indicators' endpoints and errors.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Pick a titration and find the indicators rated good: their colour change sits on the steep part of the curve.
